use_case_name: Resolve Dual Designations via Track Correlation

evidence_cards.content: The protocols in this section are to be followed in order to minimize occurrences and duration of dual designations.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This sentence explicitly defines the objective (goal) of the procedures described on the page, which is to minimize dual designations.

evidence_cards.content: The objective is to resolve dual designations by processing tracks for dual designation resolution in accordance with paragraphs 4.4.4.3.1j and k after they successfully pass the second correlation test.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This statement defines the high-level goal of the use case: resolving dual designations through track correlation.

evidence_cards.content: Track correlation prevents/eliminates dual designations.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This sentence explicitly states the high-level objective of the process (preventing/eliminating dual designations), which corresponds to the 'goal' slot for the use case.

evidence_cards.content: The recognition and resolution of dual designations require all IUs to periodically compare remote tracks to local tracks (and, optionally, to common local tracks) to determine if a dual designation has occurred.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This sentence defines the high-level objective of the use case: recognizing and resolving dual designations through track comparison.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JU must have the capability to perform common tracking in accordance with correlation and decorrelation procedures.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This establishes a required system capability that must exist before track correlation can be performed to resolve dual designations.

evidence_cards.content: All C2 JUs that originate real-time air or surface tracks shall have an automatic correlation capability.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Automatic correlation capability is a prerequisite for initiating the correlation process to prevent or eliminate dual designations.

evidence_cards.content: The system must have remote and local tracks available for comparison to determine whether a dual designation has occurred.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes the existence of the specific track types (remote and local) required to initiate the correlation process for dual designation resolution.

evidence_cards.content: Two tracks shall pass the correlation tests and restrictions in paragraphs 4.4.4.3.1f and 4.4.4.3.1g 2(1-2,1) times before the correlation is executed.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the mandatory state where tracks must have successfully passed initial validation tests (tentative correlation) before proceeding to the final execution step of the use case.

evidence_cards.content: All C² JUs that initiate real-time air or surface tracks shall have an automatic decorrelation capability.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes the mandatory system state (automatic decorrelation capability) required for the C² JU to perform track correlation and resolve dual designations.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU must recognize that two tracks being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This recognition of eligibility is the necessary system state that precedes the initiation of action to resolve the dual designation.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall make an automatic correlation test either: (a) Upon receipt of each remote real-time J3.2 or J3.3 track or J2.0 (Originator E/C = 0 or 3), J2.2, or J2.3 PPLI report which is not confirmed to have an existing correlation to a local track; OR (b) Immediately prior to each transmission of a local track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies the exact events that trigger the automatic correlation process used to resolve dual designations, directly filling the 'trigger' slot for the use case.

evidence_cards.content: The use case is triggered when a C² JU recognizes that two tracks being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This statement explicitly defines the event (recognition of correlation eligibility) that initiates the dual designation resolution process.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JU shall make an automatic correlation test either upon receipt of each remote real-time J3.2 or J3.3 track or J2.0 (Originator E/C = 0 or 3), J2.2, or J2.3 PPLI report which is not confirmed to have an existing correlation to a local track, or immediately prior to each transmission of a local track.

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the primary interaction sequence for initiating the correlation process as part of the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: Correlation testing shall consist of the position, velocity, and altitude tests specified in this paragraph. Positions of all tracks and IUs tested for correlation shall be extrapolated to the same time.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the mandatory processing steps (tests) performed by the system during the correlation attempt.

evidence_cards.content: The correlation test shall occur no more than 6 seconds after the extrapolation time.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the timing constraint for the execution of the correlation tests within the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: A local track shall be considered to correlate to the closest remote track or IU that meets all of the correlation tests, subject to the correlation restrictions in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1g and the requirement to pass two correlation tests in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1h.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the success criteria for the correlation test, specifically the requirement to pass two tests.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JU performs a Position Test by calculating the distance (D) between tracks using the formula D ≤ [a*SQRT(L² + R²) + b] dm, where L and R are positional errors derived from Track Quality (TQ) values.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the primary calculation step in the main flow for determining track correlation.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JU uses Table 4.4-2 to determine specific positional error values (L and R) based on the TQ of the local and remote tracks (e.g., TQ 15 corresponds to 0.003 dm).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Provides the data lookup required to execute the position test formula.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JU applies TQ Limitations where tracks with TQ less than or equal to a restricted value (e.g., 4) shall not be automatically correlated due to insufficient positional accuracy.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes a filtering condition within the main flow before full correlation processing.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JU performs a Velocity Test requiring the reported course of the remote track to be within f degrees of the local track's calculated course, and the speed of the slower track to be within g percent of the faster track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the second sequential test in the main flow interaction sequence.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JU performs an Altitude Test if the altitude source is valid (Sensor or Aircraft Automatic), ensuring the altitude differential is not greater than h; otherwise, altitude is not used.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the conditional third test in the main flow interaction sequence.

evidence_cards.content: When two tracks pass the correlation tests and restrictions once, they shall be deemed a tentative correlation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the first successful step in the main flow where tracks are tentatively correlated before final resolution.

evidence_cards.content: The same two tracks shall be tested again upon the next correlation stimulus.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the mandatory second test required to proceed from tentative to final correlation.

evidence_cards.content: If the two tracks successfully pass the second correlation test and there is no correlation restriction, they shall be processed for dual designation resolution in accordance with paragraphs 4.4.4.3.1j and k.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the final action in the main flow where the dual designation is resolved after passing all tests.

evidence_cards.content: After it has been determined that a common local track (TN A) satisfies the criteria of an automatic or manual decorrelation, the decorrelation shall be executed as follows: The local track shall be automatically tested once for correlation against remote tracks (not common local tracks) in accordance with paragraphs 4.4.4.3.1f and g. If the automatic correlation test fails, assign a new TN (TN B) to the local track and report TN B in a J3.2 or J3.3 message.

source_locations.location: Section b. Execution of the Decorrelation, paragraph (1)

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes the canonical success scenario for executing decorrelation — specifically, testing against remote tracks and assigning a new TN if correlation fails — which constitutes the main flow step following trigger and precondition satisfaction.

evidence_cards.content: The process of correlation consists of comparing locally derived sensor data, e.g., position, velocity, boost indication, etc., with the data received on the interface.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the core action step in the main flow for resolving dual designations by comparing local and remote track data.

evidence_cards.content: In order to eliminate dual designations, it is imperative that each ballistic missile track reported on the interface represent a single data point.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes the success criterion within the main flow: ensuring tracks correspond to unique entities to prevent duplication.

evidence_cards.content: When a C2 JU recognizes that two tracks are eligible for correlation, it shall initiate action to resolve the dual designation and transmit the J7.2 Correlation message requesting all other C2 IUs to perform a correlation of the two tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the primary action in the main flow: initiating resolution and transmitting the specific correlation request message.

evidence_cards.content: The originating JU indicates in the J7.2 message if it has any constraint which would prohibit accepting a reverse correlation using the Response Value (RV) field.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes a specific step in the interaction where the actor sets constraints on the correlation process.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs receiving or generating a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 (Correlation Rejection) shall not automatically originate a request with the same Retained TN and Dropped TN for a period of 2(1-10,1) minutes.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines system behavior during correlation rejection — part of main flow handling when automatic correlation is rejected; specifies cooldown period before retry.

evidence_cards.content: When a correlation request is rejected for a manual correlation, the JU originating the request shall provide an operator alert as a cue to conduct voice coordination.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies required human-in-the-loop action following manual correlation rejection — part of canonical success scenario’s exception handling within main flow context.

evidence_cards.content: An operator alert in the event of the rejection of an automatic correlation shall be a system option.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Clarifies that operator alerting for automatic correlation rejection is optional — defines variability in main flow response based on system configuration.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs receiving a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 3 shall automatically accept the requested correlation unless one of the following restrictions applies...
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes default acceptance behavior for RV=3 messages — core step in main flow where correlation proceeds unless blocked by specific constraints.

evidence_cards.content: The two tracks are of a different E/C, or either track has an existing E/C conflict.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: First restriction preventing automatic acceptance under RV=3 — defines condition under which main flow diverts to rejection path.

evidence_cards.content: One track is simulated and the other is live.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Second restriction preventing automatic acceptance under RV=3 — defines another divergence point from main flow success path.

evidence_cards.content: Both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Third restriction preventing automatic acceptance under RV=3 — completes list of conditions that block main flow progression.

evidence_cards.content: After acceptance of a manual correlation the resulting track shall not be the subject of automatic decorrelation processing for a period of 5 minutes.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Post-acceptance stabilization rule — ensures newly correlated track remains stable after manual intervention, supporting successful completion of main flow.

evidence_cards.content: If a correlation is found with a track for which the C² JU has R², the J7.2 Correlation message shall be transmitted with the Response Value (RV) field set to value 1 (Reverse Correlation Not Acceptable), and with the Source TN in the Header word of the J2 PPLI message as the Retained TN and the surveillance TN as the Dropped TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes an alternative successful path where reverse correlation is explicitly rejected (RV=1), diverging from the main flow’s automatic acceptance condition (RV=3). It still results in dual designation resolution by dropping the local track and retaining the remote one.

evidence_cards.content: If a correlation is found with a track for which another C² JU has R² and the TNs are different, the J7.2 (RV = 1) Correlation message shall be transmitted, with the Source TN in the Header word of the J2 PPLI message as the Retained TN and the surveillance TN as the Dropped TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This is another variant of the alternative flow: when another C² JU holds authority (R²) over a differently numbered track, the system resolves the dual designation by retaining the remote track and dropping the local one — again using RV=1 to prevent reverse correlation.

evidence_cards.content: If a correlation is found with a track for which another C² JU has R² and the TNs are the same, the JU receiving the J2 shall accept the PPLI information into its surveillance database and shall disregard the J3 surveillance data on the specified track except when Geodetic Position Quality in the PPLI message is set to value 0, in which case the surveillance track is accepted and the PPLI message shall be discarded.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This represents a third alternative flow: when track numbers match and another C² JU has R², the system retains the local surveillance track unless PPLI quality is zero — then it discards PPLI and keeps the local track. This is a successful resolution path that diverges from the main flow’s assumption of remote-track retention.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs provide a manual capability to initiate the correlation of any two tracks irrespective of standard correlation test criteria, restrictions, or requirements (such as those in paragraphs 4.4.4.3.1f, 4.4.4.3.1g, and 4.4.4.3.1h), provided that the tracks are not of a different E/C, one is not simulated while the other is live, and neither are remote.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes an alternative flow where the user manually initiates correlation, diverging from the automatic trigger and testing steps defined in the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs perform correlation tests in response to explicit correlation requests from other units, rather than initiating them automatically upon track receipt.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines an alternative entry point for the correlation process triggered by external requests, diverging from the internal automatic trigger in the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: If conflicting IDs is the only correlation restriction preventing automatic correlation, the operator may take action to change the local ID or the Exercise Indicator and ID, thereby allowing automatic correlation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines a successful alternative path where human intervention resolves a specific restriction (conflicting IDs) that would otherwise block the main flow's automatic correlation process.

evidence_cards.content: If conflicting IDs is the only correlation restriction preventing automatic correlation, the operator may transmit an ID Difference Report, which allows automatic correlation if the remote ID or Exercise Indicator and ID is subsequently changed.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines another successful alternative path involving communication with other units to resolve the ID conflict and enable the correlation process to proceed.

evidence_cards.content: When a C2 JU receives a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 0 or 1 and detects that the Retained TN and Dropped TN will decorrelate (fail the decorrelation criteria), it rejects the requested correlation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This is a successful alternative path where the receiving unit exercises judgment to reject a proposed correlation based on predicted track stability, diverging from the main flow of automatic acceptance.

evidence_cards.content: If a receiving C2 JU holds the Dropped TN but not the Retained TN, and the Dropped TN has an OCC while the received RV is set to 0, the JU transmits a reverse correlation request with RV set to 1 instead of accepting the original request.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes a specific alternative flow triggered by data ownership constraints (holding Dropped but not Retained) and OCC status, resulting in a role reversal rather than simple acceptance or rejection.

evidence_cards.content: When a receiving C2 JU holds the Dropped TN but not the Retained TN, and the Dropped TN does not have an OCC, the JU executes the correlation using the Dropped TN data and the Retained TN track number.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines an alternative processing path for resolving the dual designation when the receiver possesses different track data than the originator assumed, allowing the correlation to proceed successfully under modified parameters.

evidence_cards.content: If a correlation is found with a track for which another C² JU has R² and the TNs are the same, but the Geodetic Position Quality in the PPLI message is set to value 0, the receiving JU accepts the surveillance track and discards the PPLI message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines an exception path where the standard rule of accepting PPLI data is overridden by a quality flag (value 0), resulting in rejection of the PPLI message — a concrete error-handling condition that diverges from the main flow and alternative flows.

evidence_cards.content: Subsurface tracks shall not be correlated with IUs.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This establishes a hard constraint that prevents correlation entirely for subsurface tracks, representing an exception condition where the use case cannot proceed — it acts as a pre-filter or gate that blocks entry into the correlation process.

evidence_cards.content: Tracks with TQ less than or equal to 'e' (Restricted TQ) are not eligible for correlation, except for new local real-time tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines a specific exception condition where the standard eligibility criteria for track correlation are overridden based on the Track Quality value, preventing certain tracks from entering the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: If the speed of either track is less than 10 dmh, the 'course differential' test shall not be applied in the correlation test.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies an exception handling path within the Velocity Test step of the main flow, altering the validation logic when a specific threshold condition (low speed) is met.

evidence_cards.content: The Altitude Differential test is not applicable to surface track correlation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This explicitly excludes a portion of the main flow (the altitude test) for a specific category of tracks (surface tracks), representing a conditional branch or exception in the processing logic.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if they have an Identity (ID) difference which constitutes a conflict.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception condition (ID conflict) that prevents the successful completion of the main flow (automatic correlation).

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if they have different Mode II codes and the local Mode II code is current.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception condition (Mode II mismatch) that prevents the successful completion of the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception condition (local vs local track) that prevents the successful completion of the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if either track has the Strength field set to a value greater than 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception condition (Strength > 1) that prevents the successful completion of the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: If the received J2.2 or J2.3 Geodetic Position Quality (Qpg) = 0, the PPLI shall not be correlated automatically.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception condition (invalid Qpg value) that halts the automatic correlation process.

evidence_cards.content: If a C2 JU receiving a J7.2 message with RV=0 or 1 detects that local/remote data indicates a correlation restriction exists (e.g., as listed in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1g), it shall reject the requested correlation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception path where a valid request is rejected due to existing restrictions.

evidence_cards.content: If a C2 JU receiving a J7.2 message determines that the Retained TN and Dropped TN will decorrelate immediately upon application of decorrelation criteria, it shall reject the correlation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception path based on immediate instability of the proposed correlation.

evidence_cards.content: If a C2 JU receives a J7.2 message with RV=0 and there is an OCC on the Dropped TN, the JU shall transmit a reverse correlation if the new Dropped TN has no constraint; however, if both the Retained TN and Dropped TN have an OCC, the correlation shall be rejected.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception path resulting in rejection when conflicting constraints exist on both tracks during a reverse-correlation attempt.

evidence_cards.content: If a C2 JU receives a J7.2 message with RV=1 (indicating a reverse correlation would be rejected by the originator) and there is an OCC on the Dropped TN, the receiving JU shall reject the correlation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an exception path where a conflict cannot be resolved because the originator prohibits reversing the request.

evidence_cards.content: When a C2 JU rejects a correlation request (RV=0 or 1), it transmits a J7.2 message with the Retained/Dropped TNs set as received and the RV field set to value 2 (Correlation Rejection).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the exit action/message format for the rejection exception flow.

evidence_cards.content: If a C2 JU receives a J7.2 message with RV=3 (manually initiated), it automatically accepts the correlation unless specific restrictions apply: (1) tracks are of different E/C or have an existing E/C conflict, (2) one track is simulated and the other is live, or (3) both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines exception conditions that override even manually initiated correlations.

evidence_cards.content: The Unknown/Hostile track shall be the dropped Track Number (TN-2).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a specific state change regarding which track is dropped in an exception scenario where correlation is allowed despite conflicting IDs.

evidence_cards.content: Any JU receiving a J7.2 Correlation message and also holding OCCs on both tracks or conflicting IDs on the two tracks shall reject the correlation in accordance with paragraph 4.7.3.2a(1).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the system state after the use case attempt when specific constraints (OCCs) are present: the correlation is rejected rather than established.

evidence_cards.content: The dual designation is eliminated by establishing a single Retained Track Number (TN) and dropping the other TN; the Dropped TN is either deleted or retained as a remote track depending on specific conditions.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the final state of the tracks: one becomes the 'Retained TN' (designated as common local track if applicable) and the other is the 'Dropped TN', signifying the resolution of the dual designation.

evidence_cards.content: Specific data fields from the Dropped TN (Latitude, Longitude, Course, Speed, Altitude, TQ, Strength, and potentially Identification/IFF data) are transferred to the Retained TN upon successful correlation execution.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the data consolidation aspect of the postcondition, where the surviving track inherits relevant attributes from the dropped track to maintain continuity.

evidence_cards.content: If the own unit has R² for the Dropped TN, a J7.0 Drop Track message is transmitted, and the Dropped TN is retained as a remote track rather than being fully discarded.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies an alternative postcondition state where the dropped track persists in the system as a remote entity under specific ownership conditions.

evidence_cards.content: The dual designation is eliminated/resolved through track correlation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Directly describes the successful end state of the use case where two tracks are correlated to resolve a dual designation.

evidence_cards.content: The originating JU transmits the J7.2 Correlation message requesting all other C² IUs to perform a correlation of the two tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the final action taken by the primary actor that leads to the resolution of the dual designation across the system.
